name: PA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district lean (D+6) plus favorable environment
Houlahan's large cash advantage ($4.0M vs $0.2M) and no outside opposition
Markets price Houlahan at ~97% to win
No public polling, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: The fundamentals point clearly to Houlahan: a D+6 seat, a favorable national environment, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge with no outside spending against her. Markets agree at roughly 97%, so the forecast stays in Safe D territory with only a modest trim for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of Republican outside spending would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chrissy Houlahan seeks a fourth term in a Philadelphia-area district that leans Democratic by six points. She enters with a decisive financial advantage, holding about $4 million on hand to challenger Marty Young's roughly $200,000, and no outside groups are spending against her. Prediction markets give her about a 97% chance of winning.

Young, a first-time challenger, has not attracted expert ratings or independent polling attention, and no public general-election surveys are available. With the incumbent well-funded in a favorable environment, the race is rated Safe Democratic, though the lack of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat wider than in well-surveyed contests.
